disclaimer: Practice questions are based on common mission patterns. They are not leaked papers. Officers can ask anything. Honest, consistent answers beat memorised scripts.

questions.q: Why this country, and why this university — not a similar course at home?
questions.tip: Name two modules and a career link. ‘Europe is better’ is a refusal pattern.
questions.redFlag: Cannot name the city, tuition, or language of instruction.

questions.q: Who is paying, and where is the money from?
questions.tip: Sponsor relationship + source of funds that matches bank paper. No mystery cash.
questions.redFlag: Sponsor you barely know, or funds that appeared last week.

questions.q: What is your study gap, and what did you do in it?
questions.tip: Work, family, exams — documented. Fiction is worse than an honest gap.
questions.redFlag: Changing story between SOP and interview.

questions.q: Where will you live, and what does the first year cost?
questions.tip: Know blocked-account / proof-of-funds figure and rent band.
questions.redFlag: No idea of living costs.

questions.q: Will you return / what is the post-study plan?
questions.tip: A plausible career in Pakistan or a legal post-study route — not ‘I will settle no matter what’.
questions.redFlag: Openly treating the visa as immigration by other means.

questions.q: What language will you study in, and what is your proof?
questions.tip: IELTS clause, MOI letter, or German certificate — match the offer.
questions.redFlag: MOI for a German-taught Ausbildung, or no English for an English MSc.

questions.q: Why this course after your last degree — how do the modules connect?
questions.tip: Credibility interviews hunt subject jumps. Map bachelor → master clearly.
questions.redFlag: Accounting bachelor to ‘international hospitality’ with no story.

questions.q: How did you choose this university over cheaper options?
questions.tip: CAS sponsor, ranking honesty, and why not a similar EU public option.
questions.redFlag: Agent chose everything; you cannot explain.

questions.q: Show you understand UK maintenance funds and 28-day rules.
questions.tip: Know the published living figure for your location and who holds the money.
questions.redFlag: Funds in someone else’s account with no explanation.

questions.q: What work will you do in term time, and what is the hour cap?
questions.tip: 20 hours is typical — you are a student first.
questions.redFlag: Planning to work full-time to pay tuition.

questions.q: Why this DLI and is the programme PGWP-eligible?
questions.tip: Name the public college/university. Private career diplomas are a common refusal.
questions.redFlag: You paid a ‘guaranteed PGWP’ private campus.

questions.q: How will you pay year 1 and year 2?
questions.tip: GIC / proof of funds that match current IRCC numbers.
questions.redFlag: One year of funds for a four-year degree with no plan.

questions.q: What ties do you have to Pakistan?
questions.tip: Family, property, job offer to return to — specific, not slogans.
questions.redFlag: Entire family already planning to join on the same file.

questions.q: Who is the Ausbildung employer, and how did you get the contract?
questions.tip: Name, city, trade, start date. SK does not invent employers.
questions.redFlag: Contract you cannot verify, or ‘agent will arrange after visa’.

questions.q: What German level do you hold, and can you describe a workday in German?
questions.tip: B1 is commonly expected for nursing; other trades vary. Bring certificates.
questions.redFlag: No German for a German-language training contract.

questions.q: What is the training salary and who pays rent in month one?
questions.tip: Know the gross wage band and first-month housing plan.
questions.redFlag: Expecting the embassy to ignore empty pockets.

questions.q: Why this trade rather than a university degree?
questions.tip: Hands-on fit, not ‘university rejected me so Ausbildung’.
questions.redFlag: Calling Ausbildung a ‘easy visa’.

questions.q: What is the purpose and exact itinerary?
questions.tip: Dates, cities, who you meet. Tourism vs business must match the form.
questions.redFlag: Vague ‘visit Europe for 90 days’ with no hotels.

questions.q: Why will you return before the visa ends?
questions.tip: Job letter, family, property, studies — evidence, not a speech.
questions.redFlag: Unemployed with weak funds and a one-way story.

questions.q: Who pays, and how much is the trip?
questions.tip: Bank statements that match the itinerary cost.
questions.redFlag: Sponsor abroad you cannot explain.

questions.q: Have you been refused before? What changed?
questions.tip: Disclose refusals. Explain new evidence. Do not hide stamps.
questions.redFlag: Lying about a past refusal.
